# LaunchLoom progress update - 2026-11-16

## 2026-11-16T16:14Z Contrast glyph mask

- The pixel mask marked only visible glyph pixels, so text that matched its backdrop disappeared from the mask and false-passed. Four contrast contracts failed.
- The resolver now draws the text into an off-screen canvas with the computed font and line boxes, including input values, and unions that contrast-independent glyph shape with the visible-glyph mask. Borders, accent rules, and shadows outside the glyphs stay excluded.
- Corrected two stale expectations: the translucent-shadow input is readable because its glyphs end before the plate; the gradient case still fails at 1.84, below the 4.5 gate.
- Validation: 86/86 rendered contrast tests and 83/83 other contrast suites.

## 2026-11-16T15:17Z Approval merge conflicts

- Approving a preview whose `review/initial` branch was based on an older main failed with a raw GitHub 405: `Pull Request has merge conflicts`.
- Fresh previews now always clone the client's current `main` and create `review/initial` from it, instead of reusing the older review branch. This keeps the preview mergeable after a publication or client revision.
- The approval endpoint maps GitHub 405/409 merge conflicts to a 409 `preview_conflict` with an actionable "Generate a fresh preview" message, so the banner no longer shows a raw API error.
- Validation: `worker/test/approval.test.ts` 14/14, `tests/generation-workflow-foundation.test.ts` 19/19.

## 2026-11-16T16:55Z Fresh previews replace the review branch

- A main-based fresh preview still failed because `push-client-review-branch.mjs` refuses to force-push; it tried to replay the old approved publication commit onto main and conflicted.
- The first config push for an existing review branch now leases and replaces it from the new main-based head. Later asset/evidence pushes keep the safe script path.
- This makes the regenerated preview mergeable so approval can complete end to end.

## 2026-11-16T19:20Z Abandoned publication reservation

- Task: unblock developer approval for issue 278 and keep the fix general. Branch `codex/launchloom-publication-lease` in `/home/maigreeks/projects/.worktrees/launchloom-publication-lease`; Work OS ledger task `3488141d` with subtask `3b3dd3a5`.
- A merge attempt that fails after reserving a publication leaves a `reserved` row. `PublicationStore.held()` counted that row forever, and the alarm escalates it to `attention` after failing to reconcile the merge. Every later approval for a different review head returned `publication_in_progress`, even after the two-minute approval lease expired.
- `held()` now blocks only while a release is genuinely owned: `queued`, `running`, and `failed` always hold; `reserved` holds only during its approval lease; `attention` holds only when an approved commit, dispatch, or workflow run exists. A merge that never produced a release cannot own a newer review.
- The publication alarm now retires a reservation that is no longer the newest row, and `queue()` refuses to dispatch a superseded row. This closes the race where superseded reservation A could reconcile and queue after newer review B.
